title: Forest Resource Management
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 30S/45Q to fewer than 60S/90Q units

program.section_heading: Forest Resource Management Certificate of Achievement
outcomes: Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to demonstrate critical-thinking problem-solving skills in conservation, sustainability, and management of the forest environment.
Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to effectively communicate scientific and technical knowledge in a professional manner.
Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to evaluate scientific and technical knowledge related to forest resource management.

Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to demonstrate proficiency in quantitative skills and information management specific to their chosen field in forest resource management.
Upon successful completion of the program, the student will be able to demonstrate their professional and ethical responsibilities as leaders in their chosen field and stewards of forest resources.

notes: The catalog page renders codes without a space between subject and number (e.g. 'AGRIB5', 'FOREB11'); recorded with a space to match the closed-list format.
FORE B11 (Geographic Information Systems in Natural Resources, 3.5 units) is required in the catalog but absent from the closed list; recorded as a catalog addition.
Requirements are printed as an outer 'Forestry Certificate of Achievement (Total 30.5)' wrapping a single 'Core Courses (Total 30.5)' list; recorded as one 'all' block.

The description refers to the award as the 'Certificate of Achievement in Forestry' and the requirements heading as 'Forestry Certificate of Achievement', while the page title is 'Forest Resource Management Certificate of Achievement'.

Careers are taken from 'Career opportunities include forestry, natural resources, wildlife, parks and outdoor recreation, fisheries, rangeland and watershed technician positions'; 'technician positions' may apply to every field listed.
The source URL slug references 'summer-2025' although the catalog year is 2026-2027; reviewer may wish to confirm the version.
